newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Belarus official denies all missiles gone - agency.
newsitem.headline: Belarus official denies all missiles gone - agency.

text.p: Belarus has not yet sent its remaining Soviet nuclear missiles to Russia for destruction, a spokesman for Belarus's Security Council was quoted on Sunday as saying, contradicting statements last week by other officials.
Russia's Interfax news agency reported that the spokesman, Vasily Baranov, had told it on Saturday there were still 14 nuclear missiles in Belarus. The agency gave no other details.
Officials in Moscow and Minsk could not immediately be reached for comment.

On Friday, Belarus officials, including a senior aide to President Alexander Lukashenko, said 18 remaining missiles had gone last week -- several weeks ahead of the end-year deadline set for concentrating all ex-Soviet missiles in Russia.

Lukashenko, who is seeking new powers in a referendum on Sunday that has put him at loggerheads with parliament, had threatened to keep the a final 18 SS-25 strategic missiles as a bargaining chip against NATO's plans to expand eastwards.

Belarus, a republic of 10 million sandwiched between Russia and Poland, was the only former Soviet state outside Russia still to have missiles on its soil. They were under Russian control and could not be launched without Moscow's order.
